name: CircleCI
description: Connect your own CircleCI account to manage pipelines, workflows, jobs, insights (success rate/duration/flaky tests), contexts (secrets), environment variables, schedules, checkout keys, webhooks, pipeline definitions, triggers, project settings, and self-hosted runners from Imperal -- trigger/cancel/rerun/approve pipelines and workflows, read metrics, and run bulk operations and project health audits. Uses your own Personal API Token -- nothing is hosted or proxied by Imperal beyond the request itself. Note: covers the stable REST API v2 CI/CD domain only; Policy Management (OPA), OIDC custom claims, Deploy Components, Usage export, and Organization/Groups administration are out of scope.

tools.name: connect_circleci
tools.description: Connect your CircleCI account by saving your Personal API Token, after checking it actually works. Create one at app.circleci.com/settings/user/tokens. This manages pipelines, workflows, jobs, insights, contexts, schedules, webhooks, and self-hosted runners in your own CircleCI account/organizations.

api_token.description: Your CircleCI Personal API Token, created at app.circleci.com/settings/user/tokens.
api_token.title: Api Token

label.description: Optional friendly name for this connection (e.g. 'Personal' or 'Acme Org').
label.title: Label

tools.name: disconnect_circleci

secrets.name: circleci_connections
secrets.description: Your connected CircleCI accounts -- stored as a JSON array, one entry per account, each with its own Personal API Token and an optional friendly label. Managed through connect_circleci / disconnect_circleci -- you should not need to edit this directly.

pricing.notes: 0 = connect/disconnect/list_connections (access/credential management, no billable external call). 8 = simple reads. 16 = standard single write (create/update/delete one entity, trigger/cancel/rerun a pipeline/workflow/job). 24 = insights/audit reports (aggregated, multi-call). 40 = bulk operations across several explicit ids.
